location.ref: Vivartavilāsa, on the hidden meaning of the Caitanya-caritāmṛta

paraphrase: The Caitanya-caritāmṛta has an outer and an inner meaning; its inner meaning, known to Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja and the Gosvāmīs, is the Sahajiyā doctrine of the innate Man and of love practised with a partner.
speaker: Akiñcana Dāsa
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D

location.ref: Vivartavilāsa (and Sahajiyā manuals), on turning kāma into prema

paraphrase: Kāma (desire for one's own pleasure) is not to be destroyed but transformed: as the Caitanya-caritāmṛta says, kāma is wanting the pleasure of one's own senses and prema wanting Kṛṣṇa's; the Sahajiyā holds that prema is refined out of kāma through the discipline of the couple, as gold from ore.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
